speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik
text: asked the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (a) whether the percentage of households with utility bill arrears has increased over the past five years; and (b) how will the Ministry ensure that lower-income households with utility arrears are well supported so that their electricity and water supplies are not disrupted.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Goh Hanyan) (for the
text: Resident households that require additional financial assistance can tap on various community and social assistance schemes.

speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
text: The current U-Save rebate framework is tiered by flat type, not by household need or circumstance.

speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
text: Will the Ministry consider recognising caregiving needs as a distinct basis for enhanced utility support?

speaker: Ms Goh Hanyan
text: We all recognise that different households beyond room types may have different needs depending on the composition of their household.

speaker: Ms Goh Hanyan
text: Currently, as the Member mentioned, the U-Save rebates are organised based on room types.

speaker: Ms Goh Hanyan
text: But I do want to point out that beyond U-Save rebates, there are other forms of assistance that recognise these different caregiving needs, as explained by the responses in the earlier Parliamentary Questions related to caregiving, as well as other form of community assistance provided by, for example, the Community Development Councils.
